verses.text: These are the lands the Israelites received as their inheritance in Canaan. Eleazar the priest, Joshua son of Nun, and the family leaders of Israel's tribes assigned them their shares.
The nine tribes and the half tribe received their shares by lot, just as the LORD had commanded through Moses.
Moses had already given the other two and a half tribes their inheritance across the Jordan. The Levites received no land among them as an inheritance.
Joseph's descendants made up two tribes, Manasseh and Ephraim. The Levites received only towns to live in, with pasture around them for their livestock and space for their property.
The Israelites divided up the land the way the LORD had told Moses.
The people of Judah came to Joshua at Gilgal. Caleb son of Jephunneh the Kenizzite said, “You know what the LORD told Moses, the man of God, about you and me at Kadesh Barnea.
I was forty years old when Moses, the LORD's servant, sent me from Kadesh Barnea to scout the land. I came back and told him honestly what I thought.
The men who went with me made the people lose heart, but I followed the LORD my God with my whole heart.
That day Moses swore, ‘The land you walked on will belong to you and your children forever as an inheritance, because you followed the LORD my God with your whole heart.’
The LORD has kept me alive these forty-five years, just as he promised, since he told Moses this while Israel was traveling in the wilderness. Here I am today, eighty-five years old.
I'm still as strong today as I was when Moses sent me out. I have the same strength now as I did then, for battle and for going out and coming in.
So give me this hill country the LORD spoke about that day. You heard then that the Anakim lived there in large, fortified towns. If the LORD is with me, I'll drive them out, just as he said.”
Joshua blessed Caleb son of Jephunneh and gave him Hebron as his inheritance.
Hebron still belongs to Caleb son of Jephunneh the Kenizzite as his inheritance because he followed the LORD, the God of Israel, with his whole heart.
Hebron used to be called Kiriath Arba, after Arba, the greatest man among the Anakim. Then the land had rest from war.
